sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Wight's sago palm is a clustering or solitary palm endemic to the wet evergreen forests of India's Western Ghats. Its trunk reaches roughly 6–10 m; arching fronds can be several metres long. The plate's palm habit and divided leaves fit the species.

sections.title: Uses and caution
sections.text: Regional accounts report starch extracted from the trunk and fermented or sweet sap as uses. Fruits contain irritating calcium-oxalate crystals; reports of eating them involve preparation, but no safe preparation method is established here, so the fruit should not be eaten on this information.
